claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in its simple solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength.
The relatively low hardness and strength are caused by the absence of nanoscale precipitates.
The relatively low hardness and strength are caused by the absence of short-range ordered clusters.
Controlled aging can promote nanoscale precipitate formation or short-range ordering in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanoscale precipitates or short-range ordered regions act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
The absence of nanoscale obstacles permits relatively unimpeded dislocation motion in the starting alloy.
Relatively unimpeded dislocation motion explains the starting alloy's favorable ductility.
Relatively unimpeded dislocation motion explains the starting alloy's favorable machinability.
Precipitation or short-range ordering will increase barriers to dislocation glide.
The increased barriers to dislocation glide will increase hardness.
The increased barriers to dislocation glide will increase compressive strength.
The increased barriers to dislocation glide will reduce ductility.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the aged alloy will show statistically significant increases in hardness and compressive strength from approximately 25 °C to 600 °C.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the aged alloy will show reduced ductility from approximately 25 °C to 600 °C.
The relevant phase remains stable during testing up to 600 °C.
The comparison holds Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti at equimolar concentrations and varies only the heat-treatment-induced microstructure.
The hypothesis is limited to quasi-static testing at temperatures no higher than 600 °C and excludes processing that causes full phase separation.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mediator require formation of nanoscale precipitates, while the boundary says the alloy is processed to retain a single-phase solid solution and excludes additional secondary phases. Precipitates would ordinarily constitute an additional phase unless the intended mediator is restricted to short-range order.
